correctness.rationale: A full standard-library verifier independently reconstructs both integer three-boundaries and solves the original mod-three kernel (644 columns, rank 643), then checks a 392-unit-coordinate primitive integer cycle against every row. It proves the support criterion by exhaustion of all 644 triples; enumerates all 336 Fano graph automorphisms and compares signed coefficients. An explicit chain subdivision gives a closed 3136-unit-coordinate cycle on 9072 bisected cubes. A fresh mod-three rank 9071 bounds rational kernel rank below; the nonzero integral cycle bounds it above. Kernel saturation plus a unit coordinate proves it generates integral top H3; absence of C4 proves no quotient ambiguity. Published sufficient-subdivision hypotheses justify replacing continuous unordered configurations with the bisected cubical model. Original 392-complex is not misidentified as a deformation retract.

value.rationale: The Heawood graph has exceptional 336-element point-line automorphism symmetry, but its previously established rank-one graph-configuration top homology does not determine orientation character, any canonical cubical representative, or support structure. A striking induced-extra-edge matching rule on all 644 cells provides a natural concise characterization of a 392-unit compression, lifting to a unique 3136-unit cellular generator. The trivial full automorphism character, including dualities, and nonproduct nature reveal structural information likely useful in equivariant graph-braid computations; no claim of subdivision-independent minimality is made.
